title: MCP Failure Lab — public-safe synthetic walkthrough
note: Mirrors the private demo's shape over invented data. Every stage that shows a result restates that the result is invented, because a stage screenshotted on its own loses whatever the first one said. Total 188s (3:08), inside the 2:45-3:15 window.

caption: PUBLIC-SAFE SYNTHETIC EVIDENCE.
This demonstration uses invented implementations and synthetic
measurements. No third-party benchmark result is displayed.
What is real is the method: the schema, the scenario library, the rules.
The problem being measured: two servers can both pass a happy-path
conformance run and still disagree once the wire is malformed,
the profile is older than the requirement, or the process is killed.
The shape of a measurement — three implementations, two transports,
the real scenario library.
Which invented implementation lands where is a deterministic fixture.
Applicability is the rule that carries the project.
A requirement dated after the profile a server negotiated is never
asserted against it: NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason, never a pass,
never a failure. The same rule runs in the private benchmark.
Primary outcome and security relevance are different fields,
and confirmation is a third. No execution path writes the third.
Nothing here is a security finding about anyone — the rows are invented.
Stability is complete signature equality, not a repeated label.
Two runs that both said 'failed' for different reasons are not stable,
and this is the mechanism that notices.
Timings show every sample rather than a summary of them.
A median with the samples withheld cannot be checked for the one thing
that would invalidate it.
What was never measured is listed, not omitted, each with a reason.
A metric absent from a report is one a reader cannot tell was never taken.
It ends on what the tool refuses to say.
No ranking, no aggregate score, no best implementation.
The private benchmark that shares this schema is not represented here.
